title: MCP 2026-07-28 Spec: Stateless Core, Extensions & Tasks
content:
## Overview

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) — the open standard Anthropic released in November 2024 for connecting AI models to external tools and data — is getting its largest revision since launch. A release candidate for the **2026-07-28 specification** locked on May 21, 2026, giving SDK maintainers and client implementers a roughly ten-week window to validate the changes against real workloads before the final spec ships on July 28, 2026.

---

## Stateless Protocol Core

The headline change removes session management from the protocol layer entirely. Under the prior spec, clients tracked an `Mcp-Session-Id` header and needed sticky-session routing to keep requests pinned to one server instance. In the new spec, requests are self-contained — client info travels in `_meta` fields instead — so, in the spec authors' words, "any MCP request can land on any server instance." Practically, this means an MCP server can now sit behind an ordinary round-robin load balancer instead of maintaining shared session stores, which is the main thing enterprise deployments had been asking for.

---

## Extensions Framework

Non-core functionality now lives in a formal **Extensions** system: reverse-DNS identifiers, negotiated capabilities, and independent versioning let a feature mature and ship on its own cadence before (or instead of) folding into the core spec. Two flagship extensions ship alongside the RC:

- **Tasks** — graduated out of the experimental core into its own extension. Clients drive long-running work with `tasks/get`, `tasks/update`, and `tasks/cancel` methods, using a handle returned from the initiating `tools/call`.
- **MCP Apps** — lets a tool declare an interactive HTML UI template. The host prefetches and security-reviews the template, then renders it inside a sandboxed iframe; the rendered UI communicates back to the server over the same JSON-RPC channel the original tool call used.

---

## Authorization Hardening

Six Specification Enhancement Proposals (SEPs) tighten MCP's alignment with OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect: mandatory `iss` parameter validation, explicit application-type declaration, and stricter refresh-token guidance. These land against a backdrop of 2026 security research flagging real MCP risks in production — prompt injection via tool descriptions, tool-permission combinations that can be chained to exfiltrate data, and "lookalike tool" attacks where a malicious server impersonates a trusted one.

---

## Deprecation Policy

MCP now has a formal feature lifecycle for the first time: **Active → Deprecated → Removed**, with a minimum 12-month deprecation window before anything breaking actually lands. This gives server and client implementers advance notice instead of the ad hoc breaking changes of earlier spec revisions.

---

## Timeline

| Milestone | Date |
|---|---|
| Release candidate locked | May 21, 2026 |
| Beta SDKs published | mid-2026 |
| Final 2026-07-28 spec ships | July 28, 2026 |
| Tier 1 SDK support expected | within the RC validation window |

---

## Why It Matters

MCP adoption has grown well beyond Claude Code and Claude Desktop: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Windsurf all support it, and OpenAI and Google have committed to MCP support in their own developer platforms. Enterprise rollouts — such as Florence Healthcare's June 2026 deployment of MCP access across its application suite — are pushing the protocol into infrastructure that needs to scale horizontally, which is the direct driver behind the stateless-core rewrite.

**Migration note:** server implementations that relied on persistent `Mcp-Session-Id` state should plan to move session-equivalent data into client-supplied `_meta` fields or external storage keyed off client-provided identifiers, since the protocol layer no longer guarantees session affinity.
